documents.content:
Gauge calibration

Pressure gauges are calibrated every six months against a traceable reference. A failed gauge is tagged out immediately, and measurements made since its last successful check are reviewed.

Planned maintenance

The line supervisor approves a maintenance shutdown. Operators isolate electrical and pneumatic energy before technicians begin work. Production restarts only after guards are restored and the area is released.

Incoming inspection

Receiving staff sample each shipment using the approved inspection plan. Material with missing certificates or failed dimensions is moved to the quarantine zone and cannot enter production.

Final product release

Quality assurance reviews test results, batch records and open deviations before release. Only an authorized quality manager may change a batch from hold to released status.

Welding safety

Welders wear a rated helmet, flame-resistant clothing and welding gloves. A hot-work permit and fire watch are required when welding outside the designated booth.

Paint booth safety

Spray painters use an air-purifying respirator, chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection. Booth ventilation must be running, and ignition sources are prohibited.

Cold storage

Temperature-sensitive material is stored between two and eight degrees Celsius. The monitoring system records temperature every five minutes and pages the warehouse lead after a ten-minute excursion.

Ambient warehouse storage

Dry components are stored below thirty degrees Celsius and sixty percent relative humidity. Pallets remain fifteen centimeters off the floor, and stock rotates by earliest expiry date.

Workplace injury reporting

An injured worker obtains first aid and notifies the shift supervisor immediately. The supervisor records the event before the shift ends and escalates any hospitalization to the safety director.

Near-miss reporting

Events that caused no injury but could have caused harm are submitted through the safety portal within twenty-four hours. Reports may be anonymous and are reviewed at the weekly safety meeting.

Supplier audits

Critical suppliers receive an on-site audit every two years. Major findings require a corrective-action plan within thirty days and verification before the supplier returns to approved status.

Manufacturing change control

A change to material, equipment or process parameters requires risk assessment and approvals from engineering and quality. Validation is completed before the change enters routine production.

Product rework

Rework follows a quality-approved instruction tied to the batch record. The unit repeats all affected inspections after rework. A second rework attempt requires written approval from the quality director.

Product scrap

Scrapped units are physically identified and moved to a locked cage. Inventory control records the quantity and reason. Destruction requires signatures from production and quality representatives.
